$meta.name: e911-design-system
$meta.type: Grotesk Standard (Space Grotesk / Onest / JetBrains Mono)
$meta.a11y: WCAG 2.1 AA verified for all text/surface pairs by scripts/contrast-audit.mjs; focus indicator is two-tone (ring + halo) and scored on both tones; form-control boundaries meet 1.4.11 at 3:1 via border.control (1.5.0); Checkbox/Radio box, fill and mark audited as non-text contrast in both themes (1.6.0); status.info and status.neutral added in 1.7.0 and scored on their own soft fills — 5.55:1 / 5.51:1 light, 6.15:1 / 5.84:1 dark; the disabled tier is recorded rather than gated (1.4.3 exempts it) at 3.38:1 light and 3.27:1 dark on card; status = pill + dot + word, never color alone

brand.comment: Logo orange. Seal + ribbon gradient only; never text.

blue.comment: 1.7.0, for status.info. 5.55:1 on blue.100 puts the new tone inside the 5.14-5.58 band the other three already occupy, so it reads as a sibling. Deliberately not edge.blue #2E5FAE: an edge names a domain, a status names a state, and one value serving both would make blue mean two things on one screen.

mono.roles: dates, IDs, deltas, cert codes; tabular-nums

radius.xsComment: Checkbox box only (1.6.0). 8px on an 18px square reads as a circle and collides with Radio; 5px keeps the same corner language at a quarter of the area.

motion.durationSlowComment: 1.7.0. Scoped BY DISTANCE, not by importance: something that changes size or position. At 1.7.0 that is ONLY the rail's 64px -> 224px — Dialog and Select were audited and neither animates, and listing them here as consumers would read as already-wired-up. A colour change stays on duration; at 240ms it reads as lag, not as motion.

metric.checkSizeComment: Painted box of Checkbox/Radio (1.6.0). Not a tap target — the label row is, and it is tapTarget tall in both sizes.

fontSize.comment: Component-scale sizes that app code may need to name. The rest of the scale lives in tokens.css. The eight added in 1.7.0 were text-[Npx] literals inside this package's own components — 27 of them across 8 files, at sizes a consumer could not name, override, or lint against. Every value is the size that already shipped, to the pixel, and BOTH Tailwind ports declare these as font-size only — no line-height member. That is load-bearing: a raw text-[Npx] sets size alone and inherits the body's 1.5, so a token that bundled leading would have retightened every one of those 27 spots inside a commit whose whole claim is that nothing renders differently. What leading a 10px mono badge actually wants is a real design question and gets its own pass.
fontSize.microComment: Ribbon eyebrow and DataTable column header. SKILL.md called both 11px from 1.0.0 to 1.7.0 and was wrong; contrast-audit.mjs has scored them at 10.5 the whole time.
fontSize.tagComment: The StatusTag's word. Same 11px as label and deliberately not that token: label is the caps micro-label and carries +0.05em tracking, which would space out a short word inside a 21px pill.
fontSize.controlComment: The value inside a form control, one step down from body 13.5px on purpose.
fontSize.ribbonH1Comment: Not h1 (20px). The ribbon's title is sized against its own painted band; h1 is for the pages that have no ribbon at all.
fontSize.sealComment: The 911 lockup, the one piece of type here exempt from the contrast floor (1.4.3, logotype). Scoped by name so the exemption cannot spread.

surface.selectedComment: One step DARKER than surface.tint so a chosen row outranks the pointer resting on one. EMPHASIS, NOT THE IDENTIFIER: it measures 1.31:1 on card and 1.12:1 against the hover it is meant to outrank, so it conveys nothing alone. Waived in contrast-audit.mjs and frozen at those ratios; what gates is the carrier — border.selected at 3.53:1 for DateField, Select's check mark and label at 4.88:1. The fill is the weakest of the four signals, so nothing may be dropped on the grounds that it exists.

border.controlComment: Form-control boundary (input, Select, DateField) — 3.38:1 on surface.card, the WCAG 1.4.11 floor. Separate tier from border.default, which separates rather than identifies and stays waived.
border.selectedComment: Tracks action.primary in tokens.css — the same value, not a second decision. 3.53:1 on surface.selected and 4.62:1 on card, which makes this the half of the selected pair that meets 1.4.11.

text.disabledComment: 3.38:1 on card, 2.90:1 on surface.disabled. 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, so the audit records this rather than gating on it — the exemption is permission to be quiet, not to be unreadable, and a dispatcher still has to read WHICH action is unavailable.

status.neutralComment: Built from the warm ramp rather than a sixth hue: a neutral state should recede toward the page. It exists to give warn its meaning back — in the first consuming app, two-thirds of 84 warn tags were classification or absence, not caution — and not to let a status avoid having one. All five tones sit within 0.018 of relative luminance, so the WORD is the channel.

surface.selectedComment: One step LIGHTER than surface.tint here — same rule as light, pointing the other way because the ground inverted. Measures 1.17:1 on card and 1.06:1 on tint; see the light block.

border.controlComment: 3.27:1 on surface.card. Lighter than border.strong on purpose — this tier is an accessibility floor, not a decorative step.

text.disabledComment: warm-550 rather than warm-600: 3.27:1 on card against light's 3.38:1, so unavailable recedes by the same amount in both themes instead of disappearing in the dark one. 3.23:1 on surface.disabled.

status.softComment: Same 0.14 alpha as ok/warn, so all five soft fills sit at one weight. Flattened onto surface.card before measuring — scoring an rgba() against its own unpainted alpha reads far too optimistic.
